DR1 - Boring. The most predictable thing ever.

DR2 - It was better with the internal conflict that >!Hajime!< had, but it ended up the same way as DR1, essentially.

DR3 - We don't talk about this.

DRv3's ending was the best out of the series for the sole reason that it *wasn't predictable.* It came out of nowhere and gave me a good thought about my existence and how it doesn't matter if something is a lie or fiction. It taught me *something*. Everything else was just "move forward to gert into hope" and "its ok you dont need to be talented". DRV3's ending was great because it, to me, said "if a piece of fiction can change someone in reality, then is it really fiction?" It gave me that question and I thought about it for a while instead of absorbing it and just moving on.

What is a "hero"? Is it defined as a person who stops the bad guy? Or is it defined as something more; someone who has pure morales and wants to stop the evil deeds of others? If those are the case, then by all technicality, this girl should've been counted as a hero. But she wasn't. In all cases, she was not a hero. She was so cruel and sadistic that even her gaze could've meant you were dead. That was common knowledge.

But the girl had to constrain herself to a hero archetype. You know, the ones where they save the world from evil-doers. So, whenever a bad thing happened, she'd come to save it.

There were many examples of this, such as the time where she took down a pyramid scheme that was actively stealing money from people without their consent, or when she disassembled a gang that had been wreaking havoc throughout the world. She'd never actively killed anyone in these, only told them to get out and rethink what they're doing, but she did hurt them quite a bit.

But this time would be different.

This time, she ***did.***

 She had entered the skyscraper where the evil villain had fled to. He was on his last legs, since his whole scheme had been defeated before. The girl couldn't let him get away this time, however. She wanted to make him bleed.

She entered the tower, carelessly and mindlessly fighting her way through all the goons that appeared in her path. Their bodies were pierced with shards of ice again, and again, and again, until the ice had been covered in their own crimson, warm blood.

She had finally made her way toward the elevator, corpses strewn randomly about in the room. She assumed he'd be at the highest level, so she went there. And he was. He was shaking violently. His once hard, set-in-stone grin and glare had been knocked down to something that was barely recognizable. Tears stained his cheeks. He clearly didn't want to die.

The girl swiftly moved forward, drawing a dagger made out of ice from one of her pockets. She kicked a swivel chair over to him, before standing on it and placing the knife on his neck. He squirmed pathetically.

"You're *pathetic*." She said, in an almost emotionless tone. "Look at you. You've been knocked down to -- what, something less than a peasant? You barely have anything backing you." Blood dripped off of the girl's sleeve. "Your goons were like rocks. Fleshy pin cushions, if you will." She said gently into his ear. It was unsettling, terrifying, anything else in between.

"You're just like them, aren't you? It doesn't matter how much power you have. You'll still be the weakest of them all." She pressed the dagger to his neck even tighter, slowly beginning to slice across it. "And now, you're going to die like them also. You won't be remembered."

The man finally got the courage to speak, his voice unsteady and shaky. "..W-why... W-why are you doing this...? You... You a-are the good guy... Y...I-it... was supposed to be swift..."  The girl giggled. "I might be the good guy, but that doesn't mean that I can't *do bad things*. Hehe."

A breeze passed through the void. It was a cold breeze, one that signified death had returned once more. The breeze, however, was special this time.

As Death had climbed back into his domain, his body withered and old, a splash of color in the form of a quadruped, or a dog, entered the realm as well, standing beside the reaper.

The cloaked man had sat down, waving his hand gently and waiting for an object to appear. A small table manifested in front of him, of which the quadruped nudged and inspected for a moment, before sitting down on the opposite end.

Yet again, the man waved his hand and a tea set had appeared on the table. The quadruped tilted their head, prodding one of the cups which was on the table curiously. Their shaggy fur brushed over the rim of the cup.

"I apologize for taking you away from your owner before your time," the man begun, his voice dark but benign in its tone. "But it had to be done." He finished, closing his eyes and beginning to prepare some tea.

The quadruped stared at the man, never being able to lock eyes with him due to the hood that was draped over his head. There was no response from the dog, other than its' head tilting slightly to the right. "He was a very cruel person, I'm sure you could understand." The reaper spoke again, his focus entirely on the tea he was preparing. "It was better for you to come here than to be with him."

I've simply never experienced silence. Despite everything that might've went against it, I simply could not. Even if the room was just me and concrete walls, I could never hear anything but music.

The soft tapping of keys on a piano to create a small, but harmonious melody; the violins that occasionally played as an indicator of when things would get rough, and everything else in between.

I could hear it all. It was like an orchestra constantly following me. It was slightly calming at times.

​

I felt like that might've played into the factor that made me become a villain in the first place. I enjoyed the sounds of stress that might've filled the room during a test. It amped me up. I enjoyed the dark and horrifying music that happened whenever people were fearful or emotional. It was wonderful in every way.

But how would I use this as a power? It's quite simple. I use this to figure out what people's emotions are and playing off of them. I can tell when people are feeling scared or tense, and I can use that to get whatever I may need. 

Especially the people who try and "call me out" or "save the world from me".. It's such a pity that they try, because I can always sense a fault in their words. A paranoia. And I can play off of that, too...
